title: Divide a wardrobe into buildable modules
intro: Three bays can be built as a shared carcass or as three independent modules. The choice changes side-panel count, clear storage widths, assembly and transport, even when the front elevation looks similar.
goals: Calculate clear width under stated assumptions
Connect drawings to the parts list

sections.title: Distinguish shared and independent carcasses
sections.text: A three-bay shared carcass may use two outer sides and two dividers. Three independent two-sided modules use six side panels. Compare transport, assembly, support and serviceability, not clear width alone. Show doubled sides at module interfaces in the section and parts list; a single elevation line must not hide their thickness.
sections.caption: Three bays do not imply the same panel count in both systems.

sections.title: Calculate clear width under stated assumptions
sections.text: Exercise assumptions: three independent modules, each 600 mm externally, with two 18 mm sides. Clear width is 600 − 18 − 18 = 564 mm. Their combined external width is 1800 mm before site gaps or fillers. The 564 mm is not automatically a shelf cutting size; shelf interfaces and the connection system determine that dimension.
sections.caption: Exercise: 600 = 18 + 564 + 18 mm.

sections.title: Connect drawings to the parts list
sections.text: Assign unit codes W01, W02 and W03 and part codes shared by the elevation, section and list. The elevation shows allocation; the section explains depth, back and assembly relationships; a detail explains the joint. Record quantity, orientation, exposed edges and dimensional reference for each part. Check transport and assembly before release, avoiding duplicate shared dividers or omitted doubled sides.
sections.caption: Use the same code in elevation, section and parts list.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The drawing shows three independent modules with two sides each, but the list contains only four sides. Correct it to six sides for this design, or explicitly approve a system change and update all documents. Do not combine a shared-carcass count with independent-module drawings.
example.decision: Decision: the exercise uses six sides and 564 mm clear width per module.

quiz.question: What is the clear width of a 600 mm module with two 18 mm sides?
quiz.explanation: 600 − 18 − 18 = 564 mm under the assumptions; shelf size still needs its interface detail.

assignment.prompt: Draw the three-module elevation and section, calculate clear width and list coded side panels.
criteria: Clear width distinct from shelf cut size

faq.question: Is an elevation alone enough for a parts list?
faq.answer: No. Sections and details establish depth, back construction, interfaces and concealed parts.
